items.title: Allan Jaffe Interview, 1969-04-16
items.q: We went to Boston. We waited in the station. I remember asking George, you know, what's your commercial like?

ctx.x: No, he went away. He had a plane ticket so he flew away.

I can still get the bus if I can get a cab. Okay. If I can get a cab, I'll miss the plane too, of course. I should have left you at 12 o'clock. It's not 12 o'clock yet. I know, but I'd have to leave here at 12. So look, so you better cancel it right now before, while it's still time. I wonder if I can call in here to get a cab? Uh-huh. Well, uh, let's say I already asked you, I guess, about George's role and so on in the graphic of Preservation War. Do you, just talking about Preservation War in general, do you,…

items.title: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan…
items.q: George is happy to. George likes to play. He likes to be heard.

ctx.x: Excuse me for interrupting you here, Alan, but you said George Lewis. Now Lewis has just returned from Europe. How do you get him to come back here and play a one-night or a two-night stand?

George is happy to. George likes to play. He likes to be heard. He's happy to play with any band who he can work with. And I mean by working with, I mean, this is people who he can produce the type of music with that he wants to.

Well, did you find that you sort of got hold of a lot of extra musicians by word of mouth? Did they sort of come from the woods? Did they? Yes. Yes. I think we started out with just a few bands. In fact, when it first began, they were rotating a band once a week. And that's come to the point where we have over 20 bands and over 160 musicians that are just all seem to be falling into place. The orchestras and the bands are being more organized. At one time, a lot of the personnel were interchanging and taking…
